title: Severe ARDS lung-protective titration and early prone positioning
label: One reasonable approach
source: ARDS Network (ARMA) NEJM 2000; PROSEVA NEJM 2013; ESICM ARDS Guidelines 2023

decisions.rationale: Verify baseline PaO2/FiO2 ratio, PaCO2 and degree of acute respiratory acidosis on arrival ED settings.
Immediate lung-protective tidal volume reduction to 6.1 mL/kg PBW (400 mL for 66 kg PBW) paired with RR increase to 28 bpm to avoid volutrauma and maintain pH >= 7.20.
decisions.source: ARDS Network. N Engl J Med 2000;342:1301-8; ESICM ARDS Guidelines 2023

decisions.rationale: Titrate PEEP to 14 cmH2O at FiO2 0.8 according to the ARDSNet PEEP/FiO2 titration table (recommends PEEP 14 cmH2O at FiO2 0.8 to recruit lung units and support oxygenation).
decisions.source: ARDS Network. N Engl J Med 2000;342:1301-8; ALVEOLI Study Group. N Engl J Med 2004;351:327-36

decisions.rationale: Early prone positioning for persistent severe ARDS with PaO2/FiO2 < 150 on FiO2 >= 0.6. Note: In clinical practice, proning follows an initial stabilization period of 12 to 24 hours (PROSEVA); simulation time is compressed here for bedside teaching.
decisions.source: Guérin C, et al. PROSEVA trial. N Engl J Med 2013;368:2159-68

decisions.rationale: Follow-up blood gas to confirm improvement in PaO2/FiO2 and safe pH/PaCO2 equilibration.
Wean FiO2 from 0.80 to 0.50 once PEEP recruitment and prone positioning restore SpO2 >= 94%, avoiding hyperoxia exposure.
decisions.source: Chu DK, et al. IOTA trial. Lancet 2018;391:1693-705; BTS Oxygen Guideline 2017
